It investigates whether locally operated micro-scale robotic inspection and repair methods might detect concealed cracks, moisture ingress, damaged mechanical interfaces and environmental faults, then restore independently measurable properties without concealing failure. The core coupling is Micro/Nano Sensing x Local Repair x Structural Reliability. Every proposed integrated test is limited to unoccupied scaled habitat panels, damaged coupons, environmental chambers and supervised hardware-in-the-loop systems; no inhabited dwelling, nanorobotic building maintenance system or structural certification is claimed. The falsifiable candidate predicts higher independently verified fault recall without worsening preregistered post-repair air-quality recovery under equal inspection exposure, material supply, energy, sensing, computation, time and human-operations budgets. Repair success is separately conditional on load-path requalification, credible reference identity, moisture containment and a functioning physical stop. A controlled localized robotic repair system must compete with scheduled expert inspection, replace-on-failure maintenance and expert-performed local treatment. Concealed moisture, common-mode sensor drift, inaccessible crack ligaments, incompatible repair chemistry and hidden support fixtures are ways the hypothesis can fail. Negative specimens, refused states, destructive tests and incomplete repairs remain in the full denominator. Thirty mechanically and statistically distinct research plates include Paris-regime fatigue crack growth, mode-I and mixed-mode fracture, energy release, cohesive-interface work, load balance, fatigue survival, detection recall and false clearance, ultrasound and acoustic observability, thermal and moisture transport, contaminant mass balance, resin flow, cure kinetics, correlated uncertainty, materials and energy accounting, conditional causal effects and physically verified stop latency. Each mathematical plate states its mechanism, dimensional assumptions, independent reference, blinded contradiction and research-chapter links. The seed Paris relation da/dN = C(Delta K)^m is a conditional empirical model for particular fatigue regimes, not a universal law of repair or evidence that a crack has healed. Eighty-two chapters and 410 single-page investigations examine specimen provenance, hidden crack truth, fracture and fatigue, imaging and sensor drift, repair-material chemistry, robotic deposition, wall-module utility boundaries, environmental requalification, long-cycle maintenance and independent laboratory reconstruction. Original intake, declined parts, work in progress, consumed adhesives, repeated repairs, rejected batches and retired material remain in the denominator. Blind faults include grade swaps, hidden fatigue, wrong material passports, replayed scale measurements, contamination, source-energy omissions and optimistic virgin-substitution credits. A proposal fails whenever a load-bearing component, utility service, waste route, safety interlock or material identity cannot be independently reconstructed. This work proposes hypotheses and reproducibility obligations, not physical trial outcomes. items.summary: Unrefereed research candidate. A wide binary star takes thousands of years to complete one orbit, so its eccentricity usually cannot be found by following the orbit. Astronomers instead use the angle Γ between the pair's projected separation and projected relative velocity, whose distribution over many binaries depends on the population's eccentricity law. Hwang, Ting and Zakamska (MNRAS 2022, Appendix B) asked whether this angle distribution determines the eccentricity distribution uniquely. In the ideal model (random orbital phase, uniformly random 3D orientation, error-free projections) this package derives the likelihood of one angle in closed form, p(γ|e) = [acosh(1/e) − 1{|cos γ| > e} acosh(|cos γ|/e)] / (π sin²γ), and shows that its mixtures are classical Abel transforms. This gives an explicit inverse for every eccentricity law, including atoms: different eccentricity laws never give the same angle law. The inverse is continuous in the weak topology but discontinuous in total variation, so fine structure can be nearly invisible. Moments need no inversion: E√(1−e²) = (π/2) E sin³Γ and E e² = 1/2 + E cos 2Γ − (1/2) E cos 4Γ; these are the only symmetric unbiased single-angle observables for their targets and give near-efficient power-law index estimators. Two exact selection results bear on Gaia samples: thermal populations keep a uniform angle law under selections that ignore sky position angles, and binning by projected separation preserves the model under a log-uniform semimajor-axis law. The archive contains the 21-page manuscript (PDF and LaTeX source) with complete proofs, a Python library (likelihoods, observables, estimators, Kepler simulators), the full validation script with recorded results and figures, semantic negative controls, fast CI checks, the bounded novelty report and SHA-256 sums. All data are synthetic; no observational catalogue is analysed. Assurance boundary: written proofs; floating-point numerical checks and Kepler simulations; producer-side replay in normal and optimised modes; internal AI-assisted review (five roles, adversarial correctness review, proof audit and re-review). This is not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. Creator: Anonymous. Prose, manuscript and data CC0-1.0; code MIT.

Submission-ready reproducibility release for the PL-Seq reanalysis.

This version includes the revised manuscript source and title, complete Nature-style software references, the bioRxiv PDF build workflow, seven machine-readable supplementary tables, the renamed and updated Supplementary Figure 1 catalog, updated Figure 1 timeline, and stable Zenodo concept-DOI citation metadata.

All repository safety, syntax, and reviewed-figure checksum checks passed before release. This version adds the exact AMD64 Apptainer SIF used for FASTQ alignment, BAM processing, molecule filtering, and PSI reconstruction. The binary environment is accompanied by a SHA-256 checksum, embedded image labels, a command-derived software-version report, and usage documentation. The original Apptainer definition file was not retained; therefore, the archived SIF is the authoritative record of the executed computational environment. This version adds plseq-plotting.sif , a rebuildable Apptainer environment for programmatic PL-Seq and direct-RNA figure generation. It includes Python, Matplotlib, pyGenomeTracks, R plotting packages, Pandoc, and Poppler. The image passed embedded dependency tests, PNG/PDF artifact tests, and end-to-end rendering of the seven-page, 28-gene direct-RNA atlas.

items.summary: Supporting data and analysis code for the manuscript "Lifestyle-resolved fecal viromes reveal host-associated viral reservoirs and auxiliary metabolic divergence across animal feces". The retained dataset contains 166 fecal metagenomes (110 newly generated and 56 public), 15,106 representative vOTUs and 112 candidate auxiliary gene ORF-KO records across 105 vOTUs. The five archives provide processed data and figure sources; viral and candidate auxiliary gene sequences; the original 3,845-MAG local reference collection; assemblies for all 166 retained samples; and MAG annotation/host-comparison evidence. Raw reads are available under NCBI SRA BioProject PRJNA1454088 and the individual SRR/ERR accessions listed in the sample metadata. Version 1.1.0 is a documentation and Figure 1 reproducibility correction. It removes an unused constant input-target plotting-metadata column, provides observed QC yield fields, supplies Figure 1's required local source files, and documents the actual Holm/BH comparison families, Python-versus-R community-statistics implementations and KOfamScan-versus-DIAMOND evidence roles. Scientific sample membership, sequence payloads, abundance matrices, recorded KO calls and statistical result values are retained. The local MAG collection preserves original reference inputs, including two MAGs attributed to an excluded source sample; it is distinct from the 166-sample analysis subset. The deposit is not a newly validated one-command raw-read-to-figure workflow. Missing upstream processing/software provenance remains disclosed. The archived corrections do not certify that the separately submitted manuscript has already been synchronized. See README.txt and METHODS_AND_VERSION_CORRECTIONS.txt for precise scope and evidence.

items.summary: Pre-registered protocol (methods approved 2026-09-29; file sha256 e46e8cc4…) for a fresh-week confirmatory evaluation of frozen methods for inferring IPv6 sibling prefixes of IPv4 prefixes. Published before any evaluation-week data were read. Version 2 adds Amendment 1 (approved 2026-10-02): the published reference of validation week 20260616 is documented as an incomplete build; gates G1/V4 are decided on the three weeks with an intact reference. Published before gate G2 and before any evaluation-week data were read. Version 3 adds the freeze record (2026-10-02): gate G2 passed, reproduction check passed, code hashes frozen. Published before any evaluation-week data were read. Version 4 (2026-10-03) adds the results and the code. It was published after the evaluation: the analysis code; per-query outputs and statistics of all evaluations (E1, E2, E3); the plan, addenda and outputs of the post hoc analyses that followed E3; the completed freeze record (Steps 5–8); and a complete list of deviations and exposures with a map between the names used in the article and those of the code (DEVIATIONS_AND_NAMES.md). The method that the protocol calls the "transfer-aware rule" (code name LX3) is called the "pair-aware rule" in the article. The exposures to evaluation-week information that preceded the protocol (aggregate counts of one archive day, file listings) are stated in the protocol, section E3.0, and in DEVIATIONS_AND_NAMES.md. Not included: reference-pair tables with RIPE Atlas probe identifiers, Prefix Top Lists, and the published sibling-prefix list; README.md explains how to rebuild them. Checksums are in SHA256SUMS. Version 5 (2026-10-03) adds three post hoc items that were run after version 4 under a sixth addendum (posthoc_e3_addendum6_20261003.md): a correction of the ceiling definition, an analysis of Tor pairs that never occur as RIPE Atlas pairs, and the hypotheses without the week of 2026-07-07; their scripts and outputs; the configuration files; an updated list of deviations (items 27 to 29); and a runbook (RUNBOOK.md) with scripts that regenerate the numbers, tables and figures of the article from the released outputs. The result archives of version 4 are unchanged. The published list of validation week 2026-06-16 is called "an incomplete build" in the paragraph on version 2 above and in Amendment 1; that was the name used at the time. What was observed is lower coverage than the list rebuilt from the sources; the cause is not confirmed by OpenINTEL (see the note in DEVIATIONS_AND_NAMES.md, section 6). Version 6 (2026-10-31) adds the reproducibility extension for Sections S8–S11 of the supplement of the article “TRACE6: Tiered Ranking and Persistence-Controlled Evaluation of Probe-Reported IPv4–IPv6 Prefix Associations” (s8-s11-reproducibility-extension-v6.tar.gz), and the plans and amendments of the S8 and S9 analyses as written (protocol_history_s8_s11.tar.gz). It covers the date-matched sibling-list comparison, the overlap-cold analysis and the two-week information window (S8); the re-ranker fold-pool sensitivity (S9); the three-week E4 follow-up of 2026-09-29 to 2026-10-19 (S10); and its post hoc broker-tag strata (S11). All were specified after the E3 results were known and are descriptive. The archive holds plans, code, provenance records, saved outputs and replay commands that recompute every reported S9–S11 interval and mean and regenerate the S8 tables; it does not refit models or rebuild raw inputs. Withheld: the private-storage module of the E4 run controller (see WITHHELD_FILES.md in the archive); no reported number depends on it. README.md and SHA256SUMS are updated; all other files of version 5 are unchanged.

items.summary: This record contains the source code, trained models, and derived research artifacts associated with the study “Physical fidelity and forecasting in compressed active matter representations.” The study evaluates how dimensionality reduction affects spatial reconstruction, physical fidelity, and temporal forecasting in active-matter simulations. It compares unconstrained, physics-constrained, realizability-constrained, and combined autoencoders with proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), at latent dimensions of 128, 256, and 512. Forecasting comparisons include linear autoregression, multilayer perceptrons, and persistence baselines. Reconstruction accuracy, physical admissibility, and forecast performance are treated as distinct evaluation objectives. The archive includes: • Source code for data acquisition, representation training, posthoc analysis, frozen final evaluation, and publication rendering. • Scientific configurations and dependency specifications. • Selected trained checkpoints, POD models, fitted forecasters, latent caches, training histories, and validation analyses. • Frozen final-test outputs, comparison summaries, coverage diagnostics, and provenance records. • Numerical visual exports, software tests, and workflow documentation. The original simulation data were downloaded from The Well, specifically its active_matter dataset. We acknowledge the original simulation contributors and the developers and curators of The Well. The original HDF5 simulation files are not redistributed in this record; the repository documents their acquisition, pinned revision, and content-hash verification. The local MAG collection preserves original reference inputs, including two MAGs attributed to an excluded source sample; it is distinct from the 166-sample analysis subset. It investigates whether a frozen quantum-assisted scheduling approach can coordinate photovoltaic generation, battery storage, power converters and representative habitat service loads while preserving independently measurable energy balances and a physically enforceable safe-stop authority. The three-way research coupling is Quantum Optimization x Distributed Energy x Habitat Service Loads. All proposed tests concern isolated, unoccupied low-voltage scaled apparatus, environmental chambers, hardware-in-the-loop sources and controlled load emulators. No habitable mobile building, live human occupancy, fire or grid interconnection certification is claimed. The principal falsifiable candidate is that, with identical solar forecasts, load traces, storage capacity, computational budgets, instrument calibration and safety rules, the frozen approach improves simulation-to-bench power prediction error without increasing the number of redesigns or losing any critical protected service. The strongest baselines are competent mixed-integer energy scheduling, model-predictive control and a well-tested rule-based fallback, not unrelated structural topology optimization. Six sealed solar-load-climate briefs test cloud ramps, winter demand, overheating, outages, aged storage and telemetry failures. Hidden auxiliary supply, forecast leakage, unsafe battery reserve, infeasible QUBO decoding and unmetered quantum-cloud work are legitimate ways to refute the claim. Thirty distinct mathematical research plates develop electrical and thermal energy balances, photovoltaic current-voltage behavior, storage dynamics, charge/discharge efficiency, AC power and converter losses, protected reserves, service deficit, weather-dependent demand, rolling-horizon constraints, chance and tail-risk measures, binary scheduling, QUBO and Ising mappings, QAOA evaluation, complete quantum computation time, feasible objective gaps, locked-reference Pareto hypervolume and physical simulation-to-test uncertainty. The F38 source's DeltaHV = HV(A_new) - HV(A_base) remains a secondary multiobjective research metric; its reference point and normalization must be frozen before measurement. Each mathematical plate defines units, assumptions, a specific blind falsification and related chapters. These are established conditional relations or proposed evaluation metrics, not newly discovered laws or demonstrations of quantum advantage. These are prospective scientific objects, not fabricated instruments or completed research discoveries. Rejected runs, solver failures, negative experiments and correctly refused commands remain within the recorded study population. items.summary: A phase-only spatial light modulator in the pupil of a microscope objective can form hundreds to thousands of optical traps at once, but only if the phase pattern it displays is computed well: the pattern fixes how much light reaches the traps, how equal the traps are, where stray light goes, how the pattern survives a real device, and how fast it can be recomputed when traps move. DinHot is an open studio that runs 24 methods (19 published ones and 5 proposed here) on the same task, with the same seeds, metrics and device model, in Python as the reference and in a TypeScript port that runs live in a browser. We describe the optical and device model, the methods with the measured acceptance of each, 14 cases from a 3 x 3 array to a disordered 819-trap array and shaped potentials, the benchmark protocol, two learned models, and the 5 proposed methods, three of which meet their acceptance criteria on their acceptance tasks, each within a scope that the benchmark or the scope measurements narrow (a device-aware weighted Gerchberg-Saxton update, a flicker-bounded phase-continuous sequence and an efficiency-uniformity front), one of which meets a narrowed criterion (an aberration-robust hologram) and one of which is refuted by measurement (a learned warm start for phase-fixed weighted GS). A network trained on three-plane volumes beats its baseline at equal wall-clock on all 162 held-out volumes (median accuracy ratio 1.140), whereas its two-dimensional counterpart ties with Gerchberg-Saxton (ratio 0.9994). items.summary: Phase-fixed weighted Gerchberg-Saxton (WGS) is the practical method for large arrays of optical traps, but it optimizes the hologram on an ideal model of the spatial light modulator (SLM), and the sequences that move traps interpolate between holograms that were never optimized for the frames in between. We test two hypotheses against the strongest baselines on the same scalar Fourier model. First, keeping the WGS weights but replacing the phase update by conjugate-gradient steps through the pixel-crosstalk kernel and the phase quantizer of the device (device-aware WGS) lowers the trap-intensity spread on the device. On a 10 x 10 lattice behind a crosstalk device, the relative standard deviation falls from a median of 5.21 percent for phase-fixed WGS at 30 iterations (5.21 percent at 100) to 0.205 percent, a median factor of 26 over 5 seeds (range 16 to 33) at a median 0.995 of the baseline's efficiency; the factor is 7.9 with 4-bit phase and a fill factor of 0.85 added, and 2.0 on a smaller 8 x 8 grid with flicker added and a fixed 30-iteration budget (the ratio of the means of 3 seeds); over the 5 geometries of the studio's benchmark on that device the median factor is 1.73 (0.97 to 4.69), and 2 of them meet both thresholds. A control that removes the device model from the loop gains nothing (5.14 percent), so the gain comes from the model. Second, optimizing every intermediate hologram of a moving-trap sequence with the trap phases locked to a smooth trajectory (flicker-bounded sequence) keeps the minimum transient intensity of the moving traps at a median 0.920 of their mean (range 0.915 to 0.932) over 5 seeds at 13 frames (below 0.9 at seven frames), against 0.654 (0.551 to 0.709) for linear phase interpolation. On longer moves, with the frames that keep the peak step per frame at most 0.2 Fourier units, the bound is met on 6 and 6 of 8 seeds of two lattice moves and on 5 of 6 seeds of a rearrangement case; the seeds that miss it miss it on the phase path their end phases prescribe, and at an equal number of frames on the rearrangement linear phase interpolation leads. Both results hold in a model of a simulated device and in a transient model that we define; neither is a hardware measurement. Interactive studio and reproducible pipeline (Apache-2.0): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CEFOP_DinHot . Interactive studio: https://dinhot.fasl-work.com .

items.summary: Online sensor telemetry feeds the digital-twin, forecasting, control, and maintenance tools of instrumented water infrastructure. Probes deployed in these assets silently accumulate drift, flatlines, volatility bursts, and outages that existing pipelines often miss, because detectors and imputers are evaluated separately and under inflated synthetic metrics, and decay is treated as isolated events. This work proposes HARDIO, a Health-Aware Reliable Detection-Imputation Orchestrator, an operational data-quality framework that pairs a duration-weighted sensor decay scorecard with a per-variable, chained detector-imputer benchmark. The assignment is selected by a four-pillar composite score (operational 35%, health coverage 30%, reconstruction 20%, calibration 15%) that scores the signal an operator actually receives after detection and imputation. items.summary: Next Generation Risk Assessment (NGRA) requires the integration of increasingly heterogeneous evidence from New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), computational models, chemical information, biological mechanisms and exposure assessment. RISK-HUNT3R WP9 has addressed a fundamental challenge for this transition: how to organise, connect and reuse diverse scientific information so that it can support transparent, reproducible and human-relevant safety assessment. The RISK-HUNT3R Knowledge Infrastructure provides a FAIR-oriented digital environment for managing and connecting experimental data, methods, compounds, computational resources and mechanistic knowledge. Its architecture combines harmonised data and metadata templates, controlled vocabularies and ontologies, compound and methods databases, BioStudies and EdelweissData integration, knowledge graphs, computational tools, AI assistance resources and cloud-based services. Together these resources support the progression from data capture and curation to analysis, mechanistic interpretation and evidence integration. The infrastructure has been deployed across distributed project partners to support collaborative research and reuse of RISK-HUNT3R and legacy EU-ToxRisk resources. A central principle emerging from this work is that effective NGRA infrastructure must support more than FAIR data. Methods, models, workflows, provenance, applicability and uncertainty also need to be captured so that scientific results can be interpreted within their Context of Use and assembled into evidence supporting a decision. Resources including ToxTemp, compound and methods databases, knowledge graphs, EdelweissData and ASPA-based workflows provide complementary components of this evolving evidence architecture. The resulting infrastructure provides both an operational resource for RISK-HUNT3R and a foundation for future development. By connecting data, methods, models and mechanistic knowledge through interoperable digital resources, RISK-HUNT3R demonstrates a pathway from fragmented NAM outputs towards reusable evidence workflows supporting transparent NGRA.
items.title: From NAM Data to Trusted Evidence: RISK-HUNT3R Knowledge Infrastructure for Next Generation Risk Assessment

items.summary: 智能機器人物質驅動的自主底盤極限 13/90 ROBOTIC-MATTER-DRIVEN AUTONOMOUS CHASSIS AT THE LIMIT ROBOTIC-MATTER-DRIVEN AUTONOMOUS CHASSIS AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page high-density English research working monograph examining whether a chassis made from interacting robotic-matter modules can reversibly change its load-bearing geometry without losing structural integrity, traction confidence, actuator authority or independently reconstructable state identity. Its scope is limited to unoccupied, scaled rigs and falsifiable engineering research. Its principal hypothesis can be refuted. With equivalent materials, mass, testing time, energy, sensing and control resources, a preregistered adaptive chassis should improve traction reserve without worsening energy per mission, path error, or structural stability relative to a well-tuned fixed-geometry chassis and conservative rule-based controller. Apparent gains that vanish under actuator, controller or load-path ablations cannot be attributed to robotic matter. Thirty mathematical and physical research plates address six-degree dynamic balance, graph rigidity, stiffness and failure modes, contact-force closure, structural interface stress, fatigue, consensus, latency, support margins, power accounting, sensor covariance, fault identification and noncompensatory release. Each plate defines units, validity assumptions, an independent physical counter-test and links to substantive chapter investigations. Across 82 chapters and 410 single-page studies, the volume develops mechanical architectures, connector physics, reversible stiffness, decentralized actuation, ground interaction, reference metrology, energy integrity, wear, fair baselines and independent qualification. Two hundred Research Gates frame specific blinded perturbations, rival explanations and hard stopping conditions. Thirty-three different Phoenix Answer Embryos propose distinct tools, diagnostic instruments and successor-ready verification interfaces. This book is hypothesis-generating. It does not report a completed STARLI chassis experiment, nanoscale vehicle manufacturing, quantum superiority or passenger-safe operation. Unknown traction, unstable support, unverifiable mechanical locking, reference invalidity or revoked physical authority require stopping and withholding conclusions. Competing laboratories are invited to reproduce, refute and improve the proposals while keeping failed experiments visible. The three-coupling is Energy Networks x Distributed Power Supply x Vehicle Reconfiguration. Tests are restricted to unoccupied, scaled hardware, traceable electrical rails and laboratory/hardware-in-the-loop environments; no completed roadworthy or nanorobotic supercar is claimed. The falsifiable hypothesis is that a pre-registered distributed allocator can reduce total mission joules at the same useful task, material mass, sensing quality, energy sources, cooling, computation, time and operator budget as a properly optimized wired centralized architecture, while not worsening critical command latency. A hidden unmetered driver, local thermal hotspot, power-rail partition, stale packets, reserve deficit or failure of physical stopping defeats the claim. The supplied consensus model, dx_i/dt = -sum_j a_ij(x_i-x_j)+w_i, is used to study local agreement; agreement alone cannot prove charge conservation, battery state of charge or safe power distribution. Thirty distinct mathematical research plates examine energy-balance and signed-work integration, nodal current conservation, converter and contact losses, motor work, SOC integration and transient terminal voltage, resistor networks, rated-edge loading, droop sharing, negative incremental impedance, spectral connectivity, packet age, deadline reliability, thermal RC and Joule heating, dependent hazards, stop-energy reserve, constrained dispatch, worst-node tail risk, covariance propagation and physical safe-stop latency. Each plate provides mathematical or physical construction, dimensional limits, an individually specified blind challenge and chapter references. Across eighty-two chapters and 410 single-page investigations, the research program spans power-source custody, reconfigurable conductors, communication and consensus, electrothermal safety, fault isolation and independent qualification. Two hundred Research Gates pose distinct concealed-fault, equal-resource competitor and cross-interface problems with separate challenge, rival and stopping explanations. Thirty-three different Phoenix Answer Embryos propose experimental meters, isolation benches, duty referees, communication-energy witnesses, thermal artifacts and second-laboratory transfer contracts. These are hypothesis-forming research proposals, not completed devices or demonstrated physical outcomes.
